title: Orchestral Daft Punk: One More Loop
comment:
# One More Loop

French house played by an orchestra with no drum kit, in F minor at 122 BPM, 4/4. One four-bar chord loop runs under all 68 bars (about 2:15), and the last bar's flute run drops back into the quiet intro.

## Form

| Section | Bars | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intro (filter opens) | 1–6 | Pizzicato bass alone and growing, violin 16ths from bar 3, chops and timpani from bar 5 |
| Build | 7–8 | Timpani C pedal speeds up, violins climb, then a half-beat silence |
| Groove | 9–22 | Full rhythm section, contrabass from bar 13, horns preview the hook from bar 17 |
| Build | 23–24 | As bars 7–8 plus horns pumping C7, then the silence before the drop |
| Chorus | 25–40 | Brass hook over everything, with claps, pad, and contrabass |
| Breakdown | 41–48 | No rhythm section: pad, harp arpeggios, cellos sing the hook, flute enters |
| Build | 49–52 | Timpani accelerates each bar, cellos climb over a C pedal, horns pump C7 |
| Chorus 2 | 53–68 | Chorus louder, horns double the hook, flute countermelody |

## Tracks

| Track | Sound | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brass Hook | Brass Section | The syncopated hook in the choruses |
| Flute | Flute | Long-tone countermelody, the run back to the top |
| Horns | French Horn | Hook preview, C7 pumps in the builds, hook double |
| Violins (hi-hat) | Violin | Hi-hats: 16th chord arpeggios, off-beats accented |
| Strings (chops) | String Ensemble 1 | Guitar chops: syncopated staccato chords |
| Strings (pad) | String Ensemble 2 | Sustained chords |
| Harp | Orchestral Harp | 8th arpeggios in the breakdown |
| Cello | Cello | The hook in the breakdown, the climb in the last build |
| Pizz Bass | Pizzicato Strings | Disco bass: 8th-note octave jumps |
| Contrabass | Contrabass | Held roots |
| Timpani (kick) | Timpani | Kick on all four beats, tuned to the root |
| Orchestra Hit (clap) | Orchestra Hit | Clap on 2 and 4 in the choruses |

## Harmony and builds

- The loop is Fm9–D♭maj9–B♭m9–Csus4 into C7♭9, and the drama comes from what joins or leaves it, not from new chords.
- With no filter to sweep, velocity ramps stand in for filter sweeps, so the intro enters low and quiet and rises as parts join.
- Every build ends in a half-beat silence right before the drop.
